notes: Clear hero tile, title, value prop, three feature rows with icons; single primary CTA.
Large dead zone between the feature list and the page dots (~200 pt); content is top-heavy.
Bluetooth badge uses the success-green fill decoratively; green is reserved for LOWERED/completed.
Empty state is clear: icon, 'Find your barrier', explanation, full-width primary 'Find barrier'.
Icon-only cloud-off chip beside 'Disconnected' has no label; its meaning (local-only? offline?) is not obvious and it looks tappable.
Empty state sits low with ~350 pt of empty space above it.
State readable instantly: green 'Lowered' + flat arm illustration + 'You can drive in'.
Header block is dense (title, device+auth line, measurement caption, chip row) before the hero.
Idle STOP uses a pale tinted fill that is close to the disabled Lower button treatment; whether STOP is live is not obvious at a glance.
'Already lowered.' hint plus disabled Lower is good feedback.
Motion state is excellent: blue 'Raising', mid-travel arm, progress bar with '0.8 s of about 4.0 s'.
STOP becomes solid red and Lower/Raise disable with 'Arm is moving. Use Stop.' - correct emphasis shift.
State is clear (blue 'Raised', vertical arm).
Triple redundancy: hero 'Raised', banner 'Barrier is up', hint 'Already raised.' - the banner pushes the controls and adds little.
Lower takes the success-green fill (target-state color) - consistent with the LOWERED token.
Orange 'Stopped' + mid-angle arm is readable; both directions enabled, matching the copy.
Hero subtitle wraps leaving an orphan 'continue.'.
Banner says 'Stopped for safety' even though this may be a user STOP; wording could be more neutral.
Rejection banner is clear and actionable: title, bullet reason, plain-language fix.
'Zone blocked' chip switches to warning style - not color-only (icon + text).
Hero still shouts green 'Lowered' while the actionable problem is in the banner; Raise remains a vivid primary although the zone is blocked.
Contradiction: chip row shows green 'Sensors OK' while the hero says 'Position sensors disagree'.
Arm is drawn flat (lowered) although the position is not trustworthy; UNKNOWN uses a dashed ghost arm, FAULT should not assert a position.
The same message appears three times: hero subtitle 'Locked until it is reset on site', card 'Needs on-site reset', dock hint 'Fault latched: needs on-site reset'.
Fault card ends ~5 pt above the dock divider; cramped.
Recovery instruction (hold unit button 8 s) is clear and honest that the app cannot clear it.
Neutral surface, dashed ghost arm, '?' glyph, 'Position unknown' + 'Lower it to home the barrier' - very clear.
Lower is the only enabled primary with hint 'Lower first to confirm position' - excellent guidance.
'?' glyph floats in the headroom slightly disconnected from the arm.
Connection-lost banner with Reconnect CTA is clear and prominent; all controls including STOP correctly disabled.
'Last known: Raising' with faded arm communicates staleness, but the chip row (Zone clear, Sensors OK, 12.90 V) is still drawn in live green styles, implying fresh data.
Chip row collides with the dock divider (no bottom gap); the explanatory caption is pushed out.
Hero title 'Last known: Raising' in gray at title weight competes with the banner.
Sheet with Close, large title, one inset-grouped row (icon, name, 'Previously paired' chip, signal bars, chevron), Scan again, local-only note.
Section header 'NEARBY BARRIERS' is inset ~20 pt while every other screen insets headers ~32 pt (aligned to cell content).
Signal-strength bars have no text equivalent visible.
No scanning/empty/failed-scan state shown in this capture.
Inset-grouped lists, clear section headers, value-right rows; interlocks have icon + text.
Status pill sits beside the large title here but below it on the Barrier tab - header pattern inconsistent across tabs.
'Last counter 1' here vs 'Last counter (reported by barrier) 0' on This barrier - same field, different values.
Power card '12900 mV' caption cut by the tab bar at the fold (scroll content, acceptable).
Good empty state with icon, explanation, CTA; requirements list stays useful offline.
CTA says 'Connect to barrier' while the Barrier tab says 'Find barrier' for the same action.
Requirement IDs (C4, S5, S6) are engineering jargon for an end-user screen.
'Clear log' is a solid red filled button at the top, visually heavier than 'Share CSV'; destructive actions should be de-emphasized.
Status chips break the color system: 'Moving' is success-green (motion token is accent blue), 'Stopped' is neutral gray (STOPPED token is warning orange).
Row separators run full-bleed, unlike the inset separators in Settings/Health.
Each row has 3-4 pill chips (direction, counter, result, latency); tag-soup density makes scanning slow.
Command rows and state rows use the same blue icon styling; hard to tell event types apart.
Evidence summary wraps leaving '0.54 s' orphaned.
Inset-grouped sections, icon tiles, chevrons, disabled Bluetooth segment with lock + explanatory footer - solid.
Haptics switch uses a teal thumb on a green track (platform-default web Switch color); off-token and neither iOS nor Material You looking.
Haptics lives under 'Appearance' - misgrouped.
'Replay onboarding' icon tile uses the warning orange decoratively.
Grouped scenario list with title, description, step/FSM chips and chevrons; SIMULATED badge in nav; sticky Exit.
Sticky 'Exit presenter' bar hard-cuts the 'Sensor failure' row with no material/fade.
'FPR'/'FSM rows' jargon is acceptable for a presenter tool.
Two option cards with clear selected state (border + tint + check) and a locked option with reason.
Icon treatment differs: disabled option has its icon in a gray tile, selected option has a bare icon.
Disabled card keeps a heavy 2 pt border, so it still reads as a selectable card at first glance.
Page indicator shows 5 dots here (3rd active) but 4 dots on every other onboarding page - visible step-count inconsistency.
Clear permission primer with primary 'Allow Bluetooth' and secondary 'Not now'.
Large empty area between copy and footer.
No denied-permission state captured.
Two competing primaries: tonal 'Start 60 s timer' inside the card and filled 'Connect' in the footer.
Step 2 says 'You now have 60 seconds' while the timer reads 1:00 and has not started; the phone cannot know when the button was held, so the flow is ambiguous.
Step 2 card is cut by the footer separator mid-card with no scroll cue.
Shown after the user picked 'Try the simulator', yet it instructs holding a physical button.
Clear completion: check tile, 'You're all set.', single CTA.
Copy says 'tap Connect' but the Barrier tab button is labeled 'Find barrier'.
Spec'd 'Authenticated in X.XX s' proof is absent (fine for simulator skip path).
Native-feeling detail list, footer explanations, standalone destructive 'Forget this barrier' row in red - very iOS.
Counter values (next 1 / last 0) disagree with Health 'Last counter 1'.
Clean app-identity header, version rows, privacy and scope sections with footers.
'Firmware interface' value 'November 2026 contract' nearly collides with the label on narrow widths.
Checklist with icon + title + value; failing check gets warning icon, explanation and 'Blocked your last command' - excellent.

Several secondaries just restate the title ('Sensors valid / Valid', 'No fault latched / No fault').
Step list (Connecting, Securing, Checking owner, Ready) gives good progress visibility.
Completed step still reads 'Connecting' (present tense) next to a check; should read 'Connected'.
Two spinners at once (card header + current step).
Illustrative 'Bluetooth Pairing Request' with six empty boxes looks like a real, tappable input field inside the app.
No visible cancel/timeout state other than Close.

Raw-value column uses tiny monospaced caps (~10 pt) in tertiary color - below legible size.
Table is half-hidden under the dock on first view.
Bottom dock (segmented Interlocks/Auth latency + expand button + step label + 4 buttons) takes ~38% of the viewport and repeats the step title already in the card.
Nav row insets differ from the rest of the app: back chevron starts ~30 pt (others ~19 pt) and the SIMULATED badge sits ~12 pt from the right edge (others 16 pt).
Screen title is a 28 pt inline title, while the Presenter list uses a 34 pt large title.
